doctrine: Claude is an operating system (OS), not a chatbot. Context (95%) dominates prompt (5%) in output quality. Five core operating modes: Chat (one-off, exploration), Projects (persistent context across sessions), Code (workspaces with files/skills/commands), Cowork (autonomous desktop work), Dispatch (mobile-triggered tasks). Workspace architecture compounds value over time: Day 1 chat baseline → Week 2 Projects with custom instructions → Weeks 3-4 Claude Code with CLAUDE.md + folder structure (/context, /skills, /commands, /outputs, /plans, /reference, /.claude/agents) → Weeks 5-8 skills (reusable workflows as .md files in /skills) + commands (multi-step automation as .md files in /commands chaining skills) → Weeks 9-12 sub-agents (specialist delegates in /.claude/agents with scoped tools) → Weeks 9-16 MCP integrations (Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Notion, Perplexity, Apify, Stripe, CRM) → Month 4 Cowork+Dispatch (asynchronous background work) → Month 5+ agent teams (shared scratchpad coordination, only for 10% of projects). Skills are markdown files with name, trigger, inputs, output spec, numbered steps. Commands chain skills; one-liner invocation triggers multi-step workflow. Three-part prompt structure: Stage (who/objective/context), Task (specific action: write/analyze/build/compare/debug/rewrite/summarize), Rules (tone, format, length, inclusion/exclusion, quality definition). Few-shot examples beat adjectives. Chain-of-thought for complex reasoning only. XML tags organize long/multi-input prompts. Iterate within conversation, never restart. CLAUDE.md is 200-500 lines: purpose, who you are, how work gets done (voice/format/priority rules), what to avoid, reference file links, tool preferences. Projects upload context docs (brand guide, voice rules, pricing, SOPs); custom instructions encode voice; styles apply rules per-conversation. Memory feature persists facts across all conversations. Book writing pattern: lock outline first, draft one chapter per fresh chat, load only condensed summaries (200-500 words) of prior chapters into next chat to stay under 50k tokens, run voice audits every 3-5 chapters, condense each final chapter for future context. File upload is underused. Artifacts for content >300 words or interactive tools. Deep Research (multi-step, 50-200 sources, agentic) differs from Web Search (single-query, current info). Single agent for simple tasks. Sub-agents (hub-and-spoke, no inter-agent context inheritance) for specialist delegation and parallel execution. Agent teams (shared scratchpad) only for work requiring tight coupling/coordination (book production, full-stack builds, content repurposing across formats). Scoped MCPs per sub-agent to reduce token overhead. Each MCP server's tools consume 10-20% context if overstuffed; newer behavior offloads unused tool descriptions via internal search. Photographer practice: 15-25 total skills, 8-12 regularly-run commands, 3-6 sub-agents, 5-8 MCPs prioritized (Drive/Calendar/Gmail first, then Notion/Perplexity/Apify/Stripe/CRM). The workspace is portable IP: can be cloned, sold as productized offer, version-controlled with Git, shared with collaborators. Compounding: Month 1 slow, Month 3 visible savings, Month 6 serious asset, Year 1 one person produces at team scale, Year 2 workspace itself is productizable. Photographer-specific: The Five Stacks are Direction (on-set work), Production (pre-shoot: moodboard/location/light/pose), Revenue (pricing/proposals/invoicing/retainers), Attention (content/distribution/analytics across 7-9 platforms), and Claude (operating system underneath all four). Each Stack maps to Claude operations: Direction benefits from protocol refinement, subject brief generation, post-shoot review, skill library. Production uses moodboard builder, model research, location database, era filter, lighting library, pose starter menu skills. Revenue gets proposal generator, spec work automation, cold outreach batches, CLV tracker, financial reports, retainer client Projects. Attention achieves 4-15 pieces/day via content cutdown (one capture → 7 platform outputs), hook factory (10 hooks per post), 7x7 pipeline command, platform-specific sub-agents, analytics loop, comment/DM mining, newsletter skill. No em dashes. Field-operator voice (direct, concrete, no buzzwords/motivational fluff). Prose default, bullets/tables only when structure genuinely requires. Numbered lists for sequential steps only.

operating_rules: Context (95%) beats prompt (5%). Build the context; prompts shrink.
Chat mode for one-off. Projects for ongoing work. Code for workspace-based automation. Cowork for background autonomy.
Stop writing better prompts. Start building better workspaces.
Three-part prompt: Stage (who/objective), Task (specific action), Rules (tone/format/length/guardrails).
Few-shot examples beat adjective descriptions. Show three examples; let Claude pattern-match.
Chain-of-thought for complex reasoning only. Simple tasks do not need explicit reasoning.
Upload all relevant context files before asking questions. Claude with files dramatically outperforms description-only.
Iterate within a conversation; never restart. Restarting loses accumulated context.
Use XML tags for long or multi-part prompts: <context>, <task>, <rules>, <email>, etc.
Keep book-writing context windows under 50,000 tokens always. Condense completed chapters to 200-500 word summaries.
Start new chats for new chapters in book writing. One chapter per chat keeps focus.
Skill = single markdown file with trigger, inputs, output spec, numbered steps. Below 3 repetitions per month = not worth a skill.
Command = markdown file that chains multiple skills. Invoked as /command-name, executes full workflow in one line.
Skills are atoms. Commands are molecules. Stack them for compounding leverage.
Default to single agent for isolated tasks. Escalate to sub-agents only when single agent is clearly insufficient.
Sub-agents run in hub-and-spoke: report back to parent only. No inter-agent context inheritance.
Agent teams (shared scratchpad) only for 10% of projects requiring tight cross-specialist coordination (book launches, full-stack builds, multi-format content campaigns).
Scope MCPs per sub-agent: content-writer does not get CRM access. Operations agent gets business tools.
Overstuffed MCP list (>10 tools) degrades performance. Connect only MCPs you actually use. Remove unused MCPs quarterly.
Newer Claude Code behavior: MCP tool descriptions >10% of context window trigger internal search, reducing overhead.
CLAUDE.md = system prompt for workspace. 200-500 lines. Purpose, who you are, how work gets done, what to avoid, reference links.

Folder structure: CLAUDE.md at root. /context (background docs), /skills (reusable workflows), /commands (automations), /outputs (deliverables), /plans (roadmaps), /reference (swipe files), /.claude/agents (sub-agent definitions), /brand_assets (logos, colors, specs).
Voice rules in CLAUDE.md: no em dashes (AI tell), no buzzwords/motivational fluff, no two-sentence pivot closers, grounded field-operator tone.
Prose by default, not bullets. Numbered lists for sequential steps only. Tables for comparison across variables.
Prioritize Revenue Stack over Attention Stack when time is constrained. Cash flow first, audience growth second.
Write once, use forever: skills and commands encode institutional knowledge and become portable IP.
Version control workspace with Git. Changes tracked, prior versions recoverable.
Workspace compounds in value: Month 1 baseline, Month 3 visible savings, Month 6 serious asset, Year 1 team scale, Year 2 productizable.
Photographer specific: 15-25 skills, 8-12 commands, 3-6 sub-agents, 5-8 MCPs across Five Stacks (Direction, Production, Revenue, Attention, Claude).
Production Stack MCP priority order: Google Drive/Cloud storage first (highest leverage), then Gmail, Calendar, Notion/Obsidian, Perplexity, Apify, Stripe/payment, CRM.
Repetitive task = skill candidate. Weekly/daily ritual with 3+ steps = command candidate.
Skills take 1 hour to write initially, few cycles to refine. 10th skill takes 15 minutes. Fluency arrives around skill 10-15.
Artifacts for standalone content used outside chat: reports, landing pages, React components, data visualizations, email templates, interactive tools.
One-shot Artifacts: if prompt is specific enough, Claude produces fully functional result from single instruction.
Deep Research for multi-source investigations requiring synthesis. Web Search for current info in regular conversation.
File upload before the question in Deep Research so Claude reasons inside the material.
Do not use Claude for simple lookups, quick calculations, things you already know. Save bandwidth for reasoning work.
Memory = user-level context layer across all conversations. Projects = workspace-level context layer, distinct from memory.
Custom instructions replace first paragraph of every prompt within a Project.
Styles = named bundles of voice/formatting rules, switchable per-conversation within a Project.
Full AI-assisted (draft with Claude, edit by hand) beats fully AI-generated for publishing. Fact-check every claim. Add your voice.
Phase 1 (Days 1-7): Chat mode baseline. Use Claude daily. Practice three-part prompts. Upload context files.
Phase 2 (Week 2): Create first Project. Upload 3 context docs (brand guide, voice rules, pricing). Write custom instructions.
Phase 3 (Weeks 3-4): Install Claude Code. Create workspace. Initialize CLAUDE.md. Create folder structure. Copy Project context to /context.
Phase 4 (Weeks 5-8): Write 5-10 skills. Write 2-3 commands chaining skills. Iterate on failures.
Phase 5 (Weeks 9-12): Create 3 sub-agents in /.claude/agents. Route work explicitly. Set up auto-delegation rules.
Phase 6 (Weeks 9-16, overlaps Phase 5): Connect MCPs progressively. Gmail read-only first, expand to write. Calendar, Drive next. Add specialty MCPs per month (Perplexity, Apify, Notion, Stripe).
Phase 7 (Month 4): Enable Cowork. Test simple file task. Enable Dispatch. Send first mobile-triggered command.
Phase 8 (Month 5+, optional): Enable agent teams for 10% of projects needing tight coordination.
Phase 9 (Year 1+): Version-control workspace with Git. Audit skills/commands quarterly. Retire unused. Consider productizing.

workflows: Workspace initialization: create folder structure, write CLAUDE.md, upload context docs to /context, create empty /skills/commands/outputs/plans/reference/agents
Skill creation: identify 3+ monthly repetition task, write .md file with trigger/inputs/output/steps, test on real work, iterate until ship-ready
Command creation: identify weekly/daily ritual with 3+ steps, write .md file chaining existing skills, test, iterate, set calendar reminder
Sub-agent setup: create .md file in /.claude/agents with name/scope/allowed tools/description/system prompt, scope MCPs per agent, test
MCP connection: add tool to workspace settings, grant minimum permissions (read-only first), test, expand to write access when trusted

Book chapter workflow: outline before writing, open fresh chat per chapter, load voice guide + condensed chapter summaries (not full chapters) from /chapters + chapter outline, draft full pass in one go, iterate within conversation, condense final chapter to 200-500 words, save summary to /chapters for next chapter's context
Voice audit: every 3-5 chapters, load voice guide + last 3 chapters, ask Claude to identify voice drift, list sentences needing rewrite, fix drifts in source

Weekly content production: Sunday evening /weekly-content command chains content cutdown + hook variations + calendar assignment, Monday morning posts schedule, platform-specific sub-agents cutdown for each platform
Competitor research: /competitor-watch monthly command runs Deep Research on top 10 competitors, returns pricing/positioning/gaps/content presence

Sales/proposal generation: /pitch-prep on demand chains spec work outreach + research + concept draft + DM/email. /new-shoot chains pricing proposal generator. Both pull from /context/pricing_sheet.md
Post-shoot delivery: /post-shoot command chains thank-you + delivery note + gallery upsell + invoice + review request in one execution
Morning routine via Dispatch: /morning-briefing runs during commute, briefing ready when at desk
Content calendar + publishing: /weekly-content Sunday generates 7-day calendar with platform assignments + 80/20 split. Next week's queue is ready Monday.
Outreach batching: generate 20 tailored cold-email variations for target list, iterate winning template, scale via cold-email MCP (Instantly, Super Search, Apify for LinkedIn scraping)
Project Knowledge integration: upload manuscript folder to Project. New chapters pull in automatically. Updates reflect immediately in conversations.
prompts: Few-shot example prompt: 'Here are three LinkedIn posts that match my voice: [paste 1] [paste 2] [paste 3]. Write the next one about [topic] in the same style.'
Chain-of-thought prompt: 'Before you draft [X], first identify [prerequisite reasoning]. Then draft.'
Skill evaluation prompt for Claude: 'Review CLAUDE.md and /context. Suggest three additions based on what is missing in outputs.'
Voice audit prompt: 'Audit the voice across these chapters. Identify every place the voice drifted from [voice guide]. List specific sentences that need rewriting.'
Book blurb prompt: 'Write three book blurb variations: short (30 words), medium (80 words), long (150 words). Each leads with the core tension the book resolves.'
Competitor analysis prompt: 'Research the top 10 [niche] photographers in [geography]. Compare pricing, service structure, positioning, content presence. Identify gaps a photographer could address.'
Spec work concept prompt: 'Research [brand name]. Identify their current visual content strategy and gaps. Draft a spec image concept description. Draft the outreach DM with attached concept.'

Open-Close pattern for marketing copy: 'Generate three [asset type] variations: Variation 1 [hook A], Variation 2 [hook B], Variation 3 [hook C]. For each, include [standard structure]. Then, [role], read all three and identify which is most likely to [desired outcome]. Explain why in two sentences.'
gates: Skill candidate gate: only build if repeated 3+ times per month
Command candidate gate: only build if weekly/daily ritual with 3+ steps
Architecture escalation gate: start with single agent, escalate to sub-agents only when visibly insufficient, use agent teams only for 10% of projects requiring tight coordination
MCP gate: connect only MCPs actually used. Remove quarterly if unused. Monitor overhead.
Context window gate (book writing): keep under 50k tokens always. Condense chapters to 200-500 words.
Voice drift gate (book writing): run voice audit every 3-5 chapters. Catch drift early.
File upload gate: if relevant to task, attach before asking. Claude with files beats description-only.
Artifact gate: content >300 words or interactive tools belong in Artifacts, not chat body.
Deep Research gate: use for multi-source investigations requiring synthesis. Use Web Search for current-info-only tasks.
AI detection gate (published books): AI-assisted (draft + hand edit + rephrase flagged paragraphs + fact-check + add voice) beats fully AI-generated.
MCP permission gate: grant read-only first, expand to write only when work requires it.
Restart vs iterate gate: if first output is 70%+ right, iterate within conversation (cheaper, better context inheritance than restarting).
Project vs Chat gate: ongoing work (business, books, clients, launches) belongs in Projects. One-off questions stay in Chat.
Code vs Project gate: when skills, commands, full folder structure, or workspace becomes product, move to Code.
Name availability gate: never propose brand/product name without .com availability check + major brand/app ownership verification.
Hardest-to-say-no-to gate: every artifact = hardest thing for recipient to say no to at minimum. Study incumbent, beat on every axis. Flag placeholders.
